rounds.text: Avi Ansh Textile Ltd demonstrates compounding momentum through a remarkable 61% compounded profit growth rate over the last three years [E12]. This accelerates past the five-year compounded profit growth of 14% [E11], showing that recent structural performance is expanding at an impressive pace. Top-line expansion is actively supporting this profitability trend, with recent screens highlighting positive sales momentum through an 8% year-over-year increase alongside quarter-over-quarter sales gains [E44, E45]. Furthermore, the business maintains a steady multi-year baseline, achieving a 10% compounded sales growth rate across a five-year period [E8]. Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth sits at -28% [E13], earnings growth is decelerating [E47], and return metrics remain modest with an ROCE of 5.1% and an ROE of 3.0% [E6, E7].

The bull leans heavily on a three-year profit growth rate of 61% [E12], but completely ignores the reality that trailing twelve-month profit growth has collapsed to -28% [E13] and earnings growth is actively decelerating [E47]. Conceded: the 3-year profit figure is 61% [E12], but this short-term acceleration masks a severe 5-year sales growth of only 10% which filed statements officially flag as poor [E8, E40]. While the bull highlights recent YoY and QoQ sales momentum [E44, E45], it glosses over the fact that price growth has outpaced profit growth by 28%, meaning market expectations are aggressively racing ahead of actual delivery [E35]. Furthermore, any argument for compounding momentum collapses against the foundational return metrics of a 5.1% ROCE and a 3.0% ROE [E6, E7], which fall well below the sector median profit growth of 20.7% [E52]. Paying a staggering 108x P/E [E1] for a business with decelerating earnings [E47], a 0.00% dividend yield [E4], and a valuation sitting 17% up its range [E5] on anemic returns [E6, E7] is completely detached from the evidence.
